Football entered her life through the encouragement of her father, Renato Pires, a futsal coach. While balancing dance with other activities, Gigi spent her free evenings attending the football school he ran. What began as an experiment soon became a passion. “I started playing with the boys, grew to enjoy it, and developed a desire to become a footballer,” she recalls. item.title: Rays announce pitching plans with World Series berth on line
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays have officially announced their pitching plan for their biggest game of the MLB season. Freddy Peralta will take the mound in Game 6 of the ALCS on Monday night with the Rays one win away from reaching the World Series. Freddy Peralta will start Game 6 of ALCS for the Rays. https://t.co/IJVDbrhkba — Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) October 19, 2026 Tampa Bay enters Game 6 with a 3-2 series lead over the Cleveland Guardians after winning back-to-back games in Cleveland. The Rays now return home to Tropicana Field with a chance to clinch the American League pennant in front of their home fans. MORE: MLB history will be made regardless of World Series outcome Peralta gets the ball with the season on the line Oct 13, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta (51) reacts after pitching against the Cleveland Guardians during the sixth inning in game two of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Peralta has already been one of Tampa Bay’s most important pitchers this postseason, and the Rays are turning to him again with their World Series hopes hanging in the balance. The right-hander dominated Cleveland in Game 2, throwing six scoreless innings while allowing four hits and striking out six in a 3-1 Rays victory. He then appeared out of the bullpen in Game 4, throwing nine pitches and recording two outs. His six scoreless innings in Game 2 also came with a career-high 99.4 mph fastball, showing just how electric his stuff has been during Tampa Bay’s postseason run. The Rays acquired Peralta from the New York Mets at the trade deadline, and the move is now paying off at the most important time of the season. MORE: Every MLB team’s most recent playoff win: Which franchise has the longest drought? Rays have a chance to punch their ticket home Jul 10, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash (16) looks at the scoreboard during the third inning against Seattle Mariners at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Tampa Bay’s pitching plan becomes even more significant because Cleveland is facing major uncertainty on the mound. Guardians manager Stephen Vogt has ruled out using ace Gavin Williams in Game 6 after Williams threw 70 pitches in Game 3. Cleveland is expected to rely heavily on its bullpen, creating a potentially significant advantage for Tampa Bay. The Rays are also returning to a home field where they have been extremely difficult to beat. Tampa Bay is 58-27 at home during the regular season and postseason combined this year. A victory Monday would send the Rays to the World Series for the third time in franchise history and the first time since 2020. The Milwaukee Brewers are already waiting for the winner after capturing the National League pennant. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Red Wings' Dylan Larkin will be traded this week ESPN analyst predicts
item.description: DETROIT — Will Dylan Larkin will be traded this week? John Buccigross, the hockey guru on ESPN, said Friday, Oct. 16, on his Frankly Hockey podcast with Frank Seravalli, that Larkin will be dealt as part of a big trade. "There's going to be a trade within seven to 10 days in Detroit," said Buccigross, though not offering any more specifics as to which teams might be interested. Seravalli asked Buccigross if that pertained to Larkin, and Buccigross said yes. Larkin asked for a trade in June , but a deal was never completed when former general manager Steve Yzerman was leading the organization — and none has come close since Shawn Horcoff replaced Yzerman and was named interim general manager . Larkin had a late start to this season, suffering an upper-body injury just before training camp began, but scored a goal and assisted on another one, in his season debut . More: Red Wings hope Lucas Raymond's shootout goal will jumpstart his season A list of teams Larkin would agree to be traded to has grown to about 10 teams, though the Wings are still having difficulty finding a trade partner to meet their price. The Wings also have yet to sign restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson. Buccigross, though, predicts a deal will be reached with Edvinsson before Dec. 1, when Edvinsson would be ineligible to play in the NHL this season if he were not to sign. "I know every situation is different, but my guess is seven (years) times 10 (million)," said Buccigross, predicting a seven-year contract worth $10 million per season. "I don't know why that wouldn't get done. (Edvinsson) is off to a good start (in his career), and I don't know why he wouldn't take that. "I don't know why (the Red Wings) wouldn't offer it." tkulfan@detroitnews.com @tkulfan This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Red Wings' Dylan Larkin will be traded this week ESPN analyst predicts

item.title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Will Bolts make changes during the bye?
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers gets up after a tackle during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers fell 22-6 to the Chiefs on Sunday and at 0-6, it’s time to ask the unsurprising question: Will we see the Chargers make any changes during the bye? For the first time all season, Jim Harbaugh was non-committal to Mike McDaniel’s job security. When asked if play-calling duties would be taken from him, Harbaugh simply said, “We’ll look at everything.” It’s not much, but it’s enough to start believing the writing is on the wall for the former Dolphins head coach. Sunday’s loss to the Chiefs was the team’s first game where they did not find the end zone once and their six points were the lowest scoring output of the season thus far, as well. When thinking about the failures of this organization through six weeks, McDaniel’s lack off results is certainly up there, but the failures of this team spread far beyond just his inability to coach and teach this offense even to a serviceable level. So who do we think will be shown the door first? Who will be the first sacrificial lamb of this abysmal season? We want to hear all of your thoughts below! And now for today’s links. item.title: Why Colts fired GM Chris Ballard after Week 6 loss to Titans
item.description: Why Colts fired GM Chris Ballard after Week 6 loss to Titans originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts are currently 2-4 in the regular season, tied with the Houston Texans in the AFC South standings, and only two games back of the Jacksonville Jaguars sitting atop the division through six weeks. But following the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Tennessee Titans , the vibes for this team took a nosedive. Overall, while there might still be hope for this season, things aren't looking promising at all following a loss to the 0-5 Titans. After that loss, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported that the Colts have fired general manager Chris Ballard. While change occurring after such a loss isn't a surprise, why was Ballard the one to be fired? Well, there are a few reasons why this shouldn't be a surprise. Why Colts are firing Chris Ballard from GM role "BREAKING: The Colts have fired GM Chris Ballard @TheAthletic," Jones reported Monday morning following their Week 6 loss to the Titans. Week 6 was a brutal loss for the Colts, and Ballard paid the price. He was fired in the middle of his 10th season as the Colts' general manager. Amid a five-year playoff drought, the Colts seem headed for a sixth straight season where they could miss the playoffs. Ballard's roster construction is a huge reason for this mid-season change. Last season might've been the straw that broke the camel's back, as Ballard traded two first-round picks to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner, which was almost instantly proven to be the wrong decision. MORE : Colts fans are calling for Daniel Jones benching after ugly Titans loss Add in the extension for Daniel Jones, the bust of a draft pick with Anthony Richardson Sr., the major roster holes on the Colts' 2026 roster, especially at wide receiver following the trade of Michael Pittman Jr., and there are plenty of things to fire Ballard for. With the Colts under .500 since Ballard took over, and in a precarious spot with their franchise going into the future with no 2027 first-rounder and little to ship away to kick-start a rebuild, there's some real concern with this team Ballard constructed. There has been buzz about Ballard being fired for a few years now, and this decision from the Colts should come as little surprise. item.title: CF Montréal vs. Forge FC: How to watch, stream Canadian Championship final
item.description: CF Montréal vs. Forge FC: How to watch, stream Canadian Championship final By Cal Meachem CF Montréal host Canadian Premier League side Forge FC in the 2026 Canadian Championship final on Wednesday night, aiming to win their sixth-ever title in the domestic tournament. How to watch & stream Canada: TSN, OneSoccer USA: FS2 When Wednesday, Oct. 21 | 7 pm ET/4 pm ET Where Stade Saputo | Montréal, Québec If the aggregate score remains tied after 90 minutes, the final will proceed to extra time and, if necessary, a penalty shootout. The winner will not only hoist the Voyageurs Cup but also qualify for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup . CF Montréal Preliminary Round: 5-0 win vs. Calgary Blizzard SC Quarterfinals: 4-2 aggregate win vs. Vancouver FC Semifinals: 3-2 aggregate win vs. Vancouver Whitecaps FC Although Montréal have struggled in MLS play, they can still salvage the season by winning the Canadian Championship. In the semifinals, Montréal ousted four-time defending champs and Western Conference-leading Vancouver Whitecaps FC 3-2 on aggregate. Dani Pereira scored a long-range golazo in Leg 1, then Prince Owusu netted a brace in Leg 2. Now, Montréal are one victory away from winning the club's first Canadian Championship since 2021. Can Owusu, who has 15g/5a in MLS this season, and Chilean legend Alexis Sánchez lead the club to glory? Forge FC Preliminary Round: 4-0 win vs. HFX Wanderers FC Quarterfinals: 3-2 aggregate win vs. CS Saint-Laurent Semifinals: 2-1 aggregate win vs. FC Supra du Québec A perennial contender in the Canadian Premier League, Forge FC are in their second-ever Canadian Championship final. They also reached the 2020 final and lost to Toronto FC , 5-4 on penalties, after a 1-1 draw. That match was delayed until 2022 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Second in the CPL table (57 points), Forge's key players include former Vancouver Whitecaps forwards Lucas Cavallini and Levonte Johnson, as well as midfielder Tristan Borges. In early October, club legend Kyle Bekker announced his retirement from professional soccer. He spent four seasons in MLS (2013-16), spanning FC Dallas , Montréal and Toronto.

item.title: Blow for PSV as winger set to miss Champions League clash with Porto
item.description: Blow for PSV as winger set to miss Champions League clash with Porto As reported by VI , PSV will be without winger Ruben van Bommel for their Champions League clash with Porto. Van Bommel was absent from the PSV squad that lost this past weekend to newly promoted ADO Den Haag and has not been included in the squad list for the clash with Porto. There is not believed to be an injury concern around van Bommel, more that he is being managed having featured a lot this season having only come back from a long time off injured. The 22-year-old, who joined PSV last summer, only managed eight games for the club, with four goals in that time. This season he has picked up where he left off, scoring two goals and grabbing two assists in 11 games. His performances for PSV this season earned him a call up to Xavi’s Dutch squad, and van Bommel played in each of the four Nations League matches for his country. As a result, he has already played a lot more football in the past few months than he did last season, so clearly PSV are looking to manage him for the next few weeks. PSV lost their most recent Champions League clash away to RB Leipzig. As a result, the side travel to Porto without a win from their opening two games. They sit 26th with a single point. Porto have also started the Champions League poorly. So far the side have lost both of their opening games. Suddenly the clash between the two sides has a lot riding on it as both could do with a win to get their campaigns up and running. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 17: Kalen DeBoer of the Alabama Crimson Tide yells to his team against the Tennessee Volunteers during the first half at Neyland Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Camden Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Monday, everyone. Alabama players are focused on getting back to work after a humbling loss in Knoxville. “Got to get back up on your feet,” Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell said. “Nobody’s going to hold their head down. You hate to lose, especially this one. Big rivalry game. We hate to lose that. It is what it is. We’ve just got to keep pushing forward. There’s a lot of games left in the season. I 100% believe this team is going to go all the way. We’ve just got to put our head high and just keep going.” Russell critiqued himself and the offense plenty postgame after the offense turned the ball over four times, gained only 201 yards and tallied only 10 points, which included a touchdown that happened in the first half after the Alabama defense picked off Tennessee. The Crimson Tide struggled without starting center Racin Delgatty and star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, both out with injuries. “I had a horrible game,” Russell said. “Just put it all on myself. Couldn’t even lead my guys down the field, past the 50. I had careless turnovers. The last one was just like what the hell is Keelon doing?” If you care to revisit it, Landon Tengwall has some solid film breakdown for you per usual. Texas A&M’s roster includes offensive lineman Wilkin Formby, receiver Isaiah Horton and cornerback Dezz Ricks. The first two transferred to College Station ahead of the 2026 season. Ricks left after Nick Saban retired. Meanwhile, the man running Texas A&M’s offense is Holmon Wiggins, the former Alabama receivers coach. Wiggins is in his first year calling plays for the Aggies after Collin Klein left to become the head coach of Kansas State. This is what SBN’s Aggies site, Good Bull Hunting, wants to see from their team. Defensive improvement. Don’t look now, but Texas A&M’s pass defense is ranked No. 10 nationally. IMG Academy+ launched worldwide Monday, Oct. 19, offering families digital development resources and individualized coaching, with college-recruiting services set to be integrated into the app next year. But Ciaccio said the idea isn't simply to add another subscription to families' monthly expenses. “We were able to identify a need in a marketplace,” Ciaccio said. “Families and athletes needed expertise. We have that expertise. As the world evolved, as technology evolved, it made it easier to connect expertise with families at scale.” He compared the service to the kind of individualized help athletes and students already seek in other areas. “I see this as, you’ve got a personal coach to help you, no different than having a hitting coach, no different than having a reading or math tutor,” Ciaccio said. “I now can bring that to you in a really relevant way to help you with what you're trying to solve or get better at.” Ciaccio said families in some international markets have fewer opportunities to access specialized coaching, facilities and organized sports infrastructure. “Here in the U.S., we have a pretty well built out youth sports infrastructure,” Ciaccio said. “That does not exist once you leave the United States.” IMG's digital strategy extends beyond coaching. item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers calls a play at the line of scrimmage during an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of their Week 6 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the Green Bay Packers saw an unusual amount of movement on the point spread. The Packers opened the week as underdogs, getting 1.5 points at most sportsbooks, but the line quickly flipped to Packers -1.5 by Monday morning. Then, once the dust settled and the game approached, at least a handful of books had switched back to having the Cowboys favored. The Packers cruised, however, earning a convincing 23-13 victory to move to 4-2 on the season. That record puts them in second place in the NFC North, 1.5 games behind the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings and a half-game up on the 3-2 Detroit Lions. Both of those two teams were idle in Week 6, but the Packers have a chance to make some significant movement in the division next Sunday. Week 7 brings the Packers their third game against an NFC North opponent this season, as they will travel to Detroit to play the Lions in the late Sunday afternoon time slot. Look for that game to be FOX’s game of the week, particularly with the Packers’ recent resurgence back into serious playoff contention. However, the books are giving the Lions a reasonable advantage in this game thanks to it being played on their own home turf. FanDuel sportsbook opened the line at Lions -3.5 for next Sunday in the first of two meetings between these teams in 2026. Books are also expecting another high-scoring game between these two squads, setting the over/under for total points at 52.5. Last year saw the Packers sweep Detroit for the first time since Dan Campbell took over as Lions head coach. Green Bay took the season opener at Lambeau Field 27-13, then got another Thanksgiving Day victory in Detroit in a high-scoring, 31-24 affair. Prior to 2025, the 2020 season was the last time Green Bay went 2-for-2, when they won similarly high scoring games in weeks 2 (42-24) and 14 (also 31-24). item.description: (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Sunday, the Indianapolis Colts lost in embarrassing fashion to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. On Monday, general manager Chris Ballard lost his job. item.description: Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon promised changes to her team's leadership structure if results were not different after back-to-back 8-9 seasons. That has now happened six games into the 2026 campaign , as general manager Chris Ballard was fired Monday, Oct. 19. "Our standard is to compete for championships," Irsay-Gordon said in a statement announcing the move, "and I believe a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard." Statement from Colts on Chris Ballard being out as GM: pic.twitter.com/wFJzmkpvuQ — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 19, 2026 The final straw for the regime was a 26-20 home loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. The defeat dropped the Colts to 2-4. Irsay-Gordon said making the decision during the season was deliberate. “Waiting would only delay the important work that begins now,” she wrote. Irsay-Gordon added: “I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for the season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect to compete, improve and win football games.” Ballard had been the general manager since 2017 and was dealt the sudden retirement of Andrew Luck before the 2019 season. The team made a pair of playoff appearances during his tenure but had not returned to the postseason since 2020. The Colts started 8-2 in 2025 but lost their final seven games of the year to finish below .500. The captain trained for just under 40 minutes and then went into the dressing room with the players who had started against Leipzig. Neuer's foot will be assessed again to see how it reacts the workload and if no fluid builds up, Neuer will likely face Arsenal on Wednesday.

item.title: Mike Vrabel Has Blunt Answer to Patriots Turnover Problems
item.description: Mike Vrabel Has Blunt Answer to Patriots Turnover Problems originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Despite Drake Maye not giving up a turnover in his last two games, the rest of the Patriots haven't been as lucky. Coach Mike Vrabel believes that needs to be addressed. During Sunday’s 26-19 win over the Jets, the Patriots had three fumbles, resulting in two turnovers. TreVeyon Henderson lost the ball, while DeMario Douglas had it punched out of his hands. The Jets used those opportunities to score. "We turn the ball over at a historic rate, and it’s ridiculous," Vrabel said on WEEI’s "The Greg Hill Show" via Audacy . "It’s an embarrassment." On the season, the Patriots have turned the ball over 13 times. Seven have come via interceptions and six via fumbles. It’s the second-most behind the Chargers’ 15. The team allows the third-most fumbles, and their -6 turnover differential ranks higher than two teams. Initially, Maye was the only one to worry about after throwing seven turnovers in the first four games. However, he’s looked exceptional the last few games. The Patriots will need to tighten things up before they face the Bears on Thursday night. It’s a short turnaround game after hosting New York. The Bears rank above the Patriots in turnover differential (-2), and Chicago’s defense gives up the sixth-fewest points per game, one spot below New England. "It’s a physical football team," Vrabel said. "So we better be prepared." item.title: Alexander Volkanovski explains double retirement idea vs. Justin Gaethje
item.description: ABU DHABI – Justin Gaethje has been toying with the idea of retirement, and Alexander Volkanovski thinks it would be a fun idea to join him in a farewell fight. Volkanovski currently holds the belt at 145 pounds, while Gaethje is champion at 155. Both fighters have had legendary MMA careers in their own ways, but are nearing the ends of their fighting days with a combined 65 professional fights. If Volkanovski successfully defends his featherweight belt Saturday against Movsar Eveloev in the UFC 333 main event, the Australian would love to do a non-title superfight with "The Highlight" in which both would hang up their gloves afterward. "I even mentioned being like a retirement fight, and a lot of people are acting like I meant the next fight needs to be the retirement fight. It doesn't," Volkanovski told MMA Junkie on Sunday. "But at the same time, if that was offered to me, I go out there and do my thing and get my hand raised. "I know Gaethje doesn't really know what he wants to do. Well, maybe if you do one more, I can do that with you, and then we go out there, have our superfight, and then vacate the belts after and retire. The divisions can sort themselves out while we have our little fairytale superfight ending and sail off into the sunset. Volkanovski thinks a fight against Gaethje would sell itself. It doesn't need to be a championship fight, and he would rather have it that way. He can see himself vacating his belt along with Gaethje, and then doing one final dance. He doesn't think any division needs to be put on hold for the potential superfight. "I think that would be a cool story that's never been done, and you're not holding up the divisions doing it," Volkanovski said. "I've always said I don't want to hold up divisions. I don't think that does. Me still being a champion holds up the division because there are so many fighters that don't really deserve a fight and have to wait on who is next. If I'm out of the picture, then there's so many fights they can do for the belt. "That's why I'm like, 'Maybe the UFC wouldn't mind that.' We could do a superfight, then at the same time let all the other fights happen. I just thought that would be pretty cool and could be something. Obviously, a lot of people jumped on it and ran with it, and now I'm getting asked about it quite a bit." item.title: How Kimi Antonelli Can Be Crowned F1 World Champion in Austin, and Every Record He Would Break
item.description: Kimi Antonelli can be crowned Formula 1 world champion on Sunday, October 25, at the Circuit of the Americas. If he does it, the Mercedes driver will be 20 years and 61 days old, and he will take the youngest-champion record from Sebastian Vettel by more than three years. But the Antonelli world champion scenario in Austin is narrow: he has to win, and two specific rivals have to have bad afternoons. Here is the exact math, the engineering behind why Mercedes is in this position, and every record a title would rewrite. The short version Standings after Singapore: Antonelli 340, George Russell 238, Lewis Hamilton 229, Max Verstappen 221, Charles Leclerc 215, Lando Norris 201. Points left: six Grands Prix and no sprints, so 150 points. After Austin, 125 remain. To clinch in Austin, Antonelli must: win the race, with Russell ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower. Anything less sends the title fight to Mexico City (October 30–November 1). The Austin math: what has to happen for Antonelli to be world champion F1’s points scale for 2026 is 25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1 for the top ten, with no bonus point for fastest lap. Singapore was the final sprint weekend of the year, so every remaining round is worth exactly 25 to the winner. That makes the clinch condition simple: Antonelli has to leave Austin at least 125 points clear of every rival, because 125 is the most anyone can score across the last five races. We broke down the original scenario in our Austin clinch explainer ; this is the fuller version, rival by rival. Rival Gap now Gap if Antonelli wins Must score in Austin to stay alive Result that eliminates them George Russell 102 127 4 points (P8) P9 or lower Lewis Hamilton 111 136 12 points (P4) P5 or lower Max Verstappen 119 144 20 points (impossible behind a winner) Any result Charles Leclerc 125 150 26 points (impossible) Any result Lando Norris 139 164 40 points (impossible) Any result Why second place is not enough If Antonelli finishes second, the best case is Russell scoring zero. That leaves the gap at 102 + 18 = 120 points, five short of 125. Russell alone keeps the title open, so a win is non-negotiable. The countback that makes P9 enough for Russell Ties in the drivers’ championship are broken by number of wins, then second places, and so on. If Antonelli wins in Austin, he will have nine victories. Russell has three, so even winning all five remaining races leaves him on eight. Hamilton, on one win, could reach six. item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli can be crowned Formula 1 world champion on Sunday, October 25, at the Circuit of the Americas. If he does it, the Mercedes driver will be 20 years and 61 days old, and he will take the youngest-champion record from Sebastian Vettel by more than three years. But the Antonelli world champion scenario in Austin is narrow: he has to win, and two specific rivals have to have bad afternoons. Here is the exact math, the engineering behind why Mercedes is in this position, and every record a title would rewrite. The short version Standings after Singapore: Antonelli 340, George Russell 238, Lewis Hamilton 229, Max Verstappen 221, Charles Leclerc 215, Lando Norris 201. Points left: six Grands Prix and no sprints, so 150 points. After Austin, 125 remain. To clinch in Austin, Antonelli must: win the race, with Russell ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower. Anything less sends the title fight to Mexico City (October 30–November 1). The Austin math: what has to happen for Antonelli to be world champion F1’s points scale for 2026 is 25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1 for the top ten, with no bonus point for fastest lap. Singapore was the final sprint weekend of the year, so every remaining round is worth exactly 25 to the winner. That makes the clinch condition simple: Antonelli has to leave Austin at least 125 points clear of every rival, because 125 is the most anyone can score across the last five races. We broke down the original scenario in our Austin clinch explainer ; this is the fuller version, rival by rival. Rival Gap now Gap if Antonelli wins Must score in Austin to stay alive Result that eliminates them George Russell 102 127 4 points (P8) P9 or lower Lewis Hamilton 111 136 12 points (P4) P5 or lower Max Verstappen 119 144 20 points (impossible behind a winner) Any result Charles Leclerc 125 150 26 points (impossible) Any result Lando Norris 139 164 40 points (impossible) Any result Why second place is not enough If Antonelli finishes second, the best case is Russell scoring zero. That leaves the gap at 102 + 18 = 120 points, five short of 125. Russell alone keeps the title open, so a win is non-negotiable. The countback that makes P9 enough for Russell Ties in the drivers’ championship are broken by number of wins, then second places, and so on. If Antonelli wins in Austin, he will have nine victories. Russell has three, so even winning all five remaining races leaves him on eight. Hamilton, on one win, could reach six. That means any points tie goes to Antonelli, and a 125-point lead is as good as 126. Russell finishing ninth (2 points) leaves the gap at exactly 125: clinched. Russell eighth (4 points) leaves it at 123: still alive. The same logic sets Hamilton’s line at fifth (10 points, gap 126) versus fourth (12 points, gap 124). What changes if the calendar changes Qatar (November 27–29) and Abu Dhabi (December 4–6) remain on the calendar, and F1 has said it still plans to race both, with Imola on standby as a contingency because of the conflict in the Middle East. If both Gulf races were replaced by a single Imola round, only 100 points would remain after Austin, and the bar would drop accordingly. As of this weekend, the 125-point bar stands. Circuit of the Americas in Austin, host of the United States Grand Prix on Oct. 23–25. Photo: Spheroidite / Wikimedia Commons (CC0) The technical case: why Mercedes put Antonelli on the brink of the world title The 2026 rules reset the whole car. The power unit is still a 1.6-liter turbocharged V6, but the MGU-H is gone and the MGU-K has jumped from 120 kW to 350 kW, so electrical power now makes up roughly half of peak output. The fuel is fully sustainable. DRS has been replaced by active aerodynamics, with front and rear wings that switch between a high-downforce corner mode and a low-drag straight-line mode, plus a driver-activated overtake mode that releases extra electrical energy when chasing within a second. The cars are smaller, too: a 3,400 mm maximum wheelbase, 1,900 mm width and a 768 kg minimum weight. Under those rules, races are won and lost on energy management. Mercedes’ edge, first measured in detail in Melbourne, was less about raw hardware than about how it harvests and deploys. McLaren runs the same Mercedes power unit with identical specifications and modes, yet early-season GPS analysis showed the works car carrying more speed out of slow corners and holding it longer down the following straight, while rivals were forced to lift and coast or suffered “super-clipping,” where the battery runs dry before the braking zone. Mercedes also showed a smaller but real edge in minimum corner speed. Seventeen rounds later, that package has produced 11 wins for the team, eight of them Antonelli’s. Why COTA suits that strength The Circuit of the Americas is a 5.513 km, 20-corner, counter-clockwise lap, run over 56 laps. Three features stack up in Mercedes’ favor: The back straight. The run from the slow Turn 11 to the Turn 12 braking zone is the longest full-throttle stretch of the lap. Exit speed from Turn 11 and the state of charge entering it decide who clips first: exactly the area where Mercedes has been strongest. Heavy braking zones. The uphill stop into Turn 1, plus Turns 11 and 12, are prime MGU-K harvesting points. A car that recovers efficiently there can deploy more aggressively everywhere else. The Esses. The fast Turns 3–6 sequence rewards a stable aero platform in corner mode, and the transition back to straight-line mode is where active-aero calibration shows. The counterweight is Ferrari, which is bringing a new floor and sidepods to Austin. Hamilton is the more dangerous Ferrari in the standings, and his line is fifth place. For context on how Ferrari’s strategy split cost him in Singapore, see our Singapore strategy analysis . Red Bull Ford’s late-season surge, including Verstappen’s Singapore win , is real, but even a Verstappen victory cannot keep him alive if Antonelli finishes ahead of him. We looked at what Red Bull’s engine numbers do and do not show in our ADUO benchmark piece . The risks that could stop it Russell. The teammate is the whole scenario. Same car, same energy maps, and he only needs eighth. His next engine penalty is expected at Las Vegas, not Austin. More on that in our Russell penalty explainer . Turn 1. The wide, uphill first corner invites dive-bombs on lap one. A first-lap incident is the most likely way the scenario collapses. Safety cars and strategy. A badly timed neutralization can turn a lead into a lost win, and a winner-or-nothing target leaves no margin. Reliability. One power unit problem ends the Austin clinch outright and hands Russell 25 points of breathing room. Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, 2025 Singapore GP FP2. Photo: Liauzh via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. Every record Antonelli would break as world champion Record Antonelli (Austin clinch) Current holder Youngest F1 world champion 20 years, 61 days Sebastian Vettel, 23 years, 134 days (2010) First Italian champion in 73 years 2026 Alberto Ascari (1952, 1953) First Italian champion with a non-Italian team Mercedes Giuseppe Farina (Alfa Romeo), Ascari (Ferrari) First champion born in the 2000s Born August 25, 2006 Lando Norris, born 1999 First drivers’ title for Mercedes since 2020 2026 Lewis Hamilton (2020) The age record is the headline, and it is a big one. Vettel’s mark stood for 16 years; Hamilton (23 years, 300 days in 2008) and Fernando Alonso (24 years, 58 days in 2005) are the only others to have won before turning 25. As we explained in our deep dive on the age record , the FIA’s Super Licence age rules make it unusually hard for anyone to take it back. Antonelli would also become only the third Italian world champion, after Farina, the sport’s first champion in 1950, and Ascari. A title would follow the youngest-ever records he already holds for leading the championship (19 years, 216 days, after Japan) and for a Grand Prix pole position (China). Records

item.title: ‘Not going to deny’ – Ronald Araujo makes honest admission about playing right-back for Liverpool
item.description: ‘Not going to deny’ – Ronald Araujo makes honest admission about playing right-back for Liverpool Ronald Araujo has spoken candidly about playing primarily as a right-back in his first few appearances for Liverpool. The Uruguay defender joined the Reds on loan from Barcelona in August, with the option to make the transfer permanent if they desire, and reports from Spain suggest that Anfield chiefs already want to activate that clause for the 27-year-old. He was initially signed with a view to adding centre-back depth at a time when Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez were sidelined, and Virgil van Dijk was only coming back to club duties after the World Cup, but he’s played mostly on the right so far under Andoni Iraola. Araujo was prepared to play at right-back Araujo spoke to the media on Monday afternoon ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League clash against Villarreal tomorrow night, and he was open to the possibility of being asked to play at right-back when he came to Anfield. The Uruguayan said (via Liverpool Echo ): “It’s not a problem as I’d already played there a few times. “When I made the decision to come here, I knew it was one of the possibilities to play as a right-back, so it’s not something so different for me. Ultimately I try to give everything I can, no matter what position I am in or what the manager asks. “I’m not going to deny that I feel more comfortbale at centre-back, but at the end of the day [right-back] is not a difficult position for me.” (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Araujo’s versatility has helped Liverpool massively Araujo has played at right-back for Liverpool largely out of necessity, with Conor Bradley still sidelined with a long-term injury and Jeremie Frimpong now joining him in the treatment room. The 27-year-old has immediately endeared himself to the Anfield faithful with a series of solid performances and his heart-on-his-sleeve nature, and his ability to provide strong cover on the right has been huge for the Reds. Whereas Arne Slot felt compelled to utilise midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones as emergency right-backs on several occasions last season, Iraola has the benefit of calling upon an actual defender to fill that position. With the new centre-back partnership of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet flourishing, Araujo’s best chance of keeping his place in the starting XI would probably be on the right, where Liverpool now have neither of their natural senior options available. The Uruguayan might feel more at home in the centre of defence, but his readiness to play at right-back has been instrumental in his team having a steady start to the campaign when it could easily have been chaotic.

item.title: End of an era for disabled gymnastics competition
item.description: Veronica, 11, said the event was "a chance to shine" [BBC] A gymnastic competition for people with disabilities may have come to an end after 26 years. The annual event welcomed competitors from across Europe to Poole, Dorset, over the weekend. However, organisers Kay Salter MBE and Dave Balmer, both aged in their 80s, have decided to step down. Balmer said they were both "incredibly proud" to see the gymnasts' progress over the years and hoped the event would continue under new leadership. He said: "When we started this competition in 2000, we simply wanted to give lower-level disability gymnasts the chance to compete and enjoy the sport they love. "We never imagined it would still be going more than 25 years later. "What means the most to me is seeing competitors who first walked through our doors as young children now taking part in the adult categories." Organiser Kay Salter MBE said she was "very, very emotional" at her final event [BBC] Salter said she felt "very, very emotional" at the final event. "I don't want it to be the end," she said. "It's been such a tremendous success that gymnasts are already asking me, 'When's the competition next year?' and I can't tell them." About 100 gymnasts took part in the Poole Disabled Open Gymnastics Competition at Rossmore Leisure Centre, which was originally funded by BBC Children in Need. Veronica, 11, who performed a floor routine, said: "One day when I grow up, I can show all other disability people just like me that they can do anything. "It's important for other people to have a chance to shine." The annual event has been running since the year 2000 [BBC] See also The gymnast so successful she lost count of her medals Young gymnast campaigning to see her sport at the Paralympics

item.title: PSG vs Barcelona update issued as violent protests in France threaten Champions League clash
item.description: The Champions League fixture between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona will be played as scheduled on Tuesday at the Parc des Princes , the French Interior minister has confirmed. The decision comes after a weekend of protests across France that were marred by violence and looting. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez spoke after an emergency meeting with top government officials, at which the possibility of calling off planned events, including football matches, was discussed. “But this does not apply to tomorrow’s match between PSG and FC Barcelona,” he said, adding that other matches planned in European competitions this week would not be affected. Among the fixtures still going ahead, he mentioned the match between Lille and Galatasaray scheduled for Wednesday in the northern city, where looters also vandalised shops over the weekend. Laurent Nunez has confirmed Tuesday's match will go ahead (AP) The violence of recent days targeted city halls, other public buildings and hundreds of businesses across the country. More than 2,000 arrests have been made in connection with the unrest. Images of the violence have drawn worldwide attention and left many French citizens shocked, highlighting the country's tense social climate. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he has instructed prefects to impose “very limited” and “localised” curfews in cities to prevent more rioting and looting. Lecornu said details of the areas to be placed under curfew will be provided later. Nuñez acknowledged that authorities had “lost control” in some major cities on Saturday, with hundreds of businesses looted. Nuñez offered his resignation on Sunday, but French President Emmanuel Macron asked him to stay to respond to police needs in an emergency situation. Macron instructed Nuñez “to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence.” Tuesday's match at the Parc des Princes will require a robust security deployment, with police forces already strained following weeks of student protests. In May, Paris police detained dozens of people after violence disrupted celebrations of PSG's second successive Champions League triumph following a penalty shootout win over Arsenal, and a group tried to storm a police station in the French capital.

Once hyped as possibly the greatest prospect in US men’s history, a series of injuries kept him from simply taking the field, much less making his mark on it. Since his emergent 2020-21 season, when he logged nearly 2,000 Bundesliga minutes running alongside Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, and Jadon Sancho, Reyna finished each of the ensuing five seasons without even cresting 630 league minutes. “Rotational” became a generous descriptor for his role at Nottingham Forest on loan, and then last season with Borussia Mönchengladbach. Still, Gregg Berhalter and Mauricio Pochettino kept involving Reyna with the US squad based on that pesky potential – betting that, on his day, he still had the raw talent to do what few compatriots could. item.title: Another unremarkable win shows Arsenal’s strength is in depth rather than creativity | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Champions so risk-averse Forest were lured into thinking they had a chance, until bench was used to see them off Pass. Pass. Pass. Pass. Sideways. Square. Backwards. Pass. Pass. Recycle. Pass. It wasn’t much of a spectacle. But in the end, for the second week running, thanks in no small part of their bench, Arsenal won. Fireworks in the autumn are for Bonfire Night; titles require relentless accumulation. Since the international break, Arsenal have won three games out of three despite not being in the lead at half-time in any of them. Hammered at Brighton and having endured a drab first hour at home to Leeds last week, there has been a rare sense, for the first time really since Manchester City dropped points at Everton at the beginning of May, of Arsenal not being quite at their best, needing to reassert their quality. This was not a performance that would terrify any opponent, but it did highlight Arsenal’s consistency and it did demonstrate just how deep their squad now runs. Continue reading...

item.title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace
item.description: At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season. Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
